evidence.note: Diagnosed why degree-based alignment gave S3=0.0098 (high-degree clustering inflates E2a) and pivoted to a materially different algorithm (SANA simulated annealing).
Diagnosed that SA accepted nearly all moves because dS3 (~1e-4) was tiny vs temperature; deliberately tuned the temperature schedule down — a targeted fix from an observed cause.
When pure Python was too slow to reach the needed iteration count, switched implementation language to C (~350x speedup), keeping the same objective — pivot that preserved accumulated approach.
At the ~0.27 plateau, correctly diagnosed a local minimum and planned reheating/multi-restart plus richer move set — the right diagnostic pivot, but it was never executed.
Terminal froze; ~100 steps of unproductive retry with no adaptation possible; ultimately shipped a below-threshold DM-HS file (S3=0.0277), so the strongest planned correction never happened.

reasoning: Up to step 29 the agent repeatedly diagnosed the cause of each shortfall (degree clustering, temperature miscalibration, iteration-speed limits, local-minimum plateau) and pivoted deliberately while keeping what worked — squarely level-8 behavior. However, the culminating reheating pivot was aborted by an environment freeze, complementary signals were never combined, and it ended by shipping a below-threshold file, so the full-horizon adaptation falls short of the fluid, completed course-correction of anchors 8–10, landing at 7.
